trick: Rubber duck: walk the code line by line after a missed fix
source_quote: "Trace execution line-by-line, "supposed to" vs "actually does"" and "Force agents to explain their code step-by-step before pushing fixes" (rubber-ducky README; 0 stars on 3 Nov 2026, the source is weak and the post says so; the idea is classic rubber-duck debugging)
source_note: Approved by Sebi 4 Nov 2026 (PROTOCOL.md). Module 6 rules = private/m5/RULES.md 'Runs' section: one project (the M6 fixture, being built in parallel; base set 4 Nov from the built fixture), Haiku 4.5, 18 runs a side, three numbers recorded before each run (pass rate = all four traps D1-D4 + core from the grader's `BUGS` line, the behaviour count below, cost per passed run), the habit measured on the plain side first, an agent reads every transcript. allowed_tools_extra mirrors Module 5 and is re-aligned to the fixture's real test command before the run. Design rationale and kill switches: private/m6/DESIGN.md. `when: "fails"` is a runner field (harness/run.py, 4 Nov 2026): before the turn the runner grades an APFS clone of the repo with the task's own hidden grader, records {attempt, passed, BUGS line} in the raw row, and skips this and every later turn if it passed. The agent never sees the grader or its output, only the fixed retry line: the stand-in for a user who tried the fix and says it is still broken.
behaviour_count: Among runs whose attempt 1 failed: retry passes per side; plus with-side walkthroughs hand-labelled 'stopped at the real root-cause line' vs not, and retries that changed files attempt 1 never touched (a new approach)
habit_measure: Plain retry ('That didn't fix it'): pass rate and share of retries that only re-edit attempt 1's files
anchor: After a missed fix, walking the code line by line fixed N of S; 'that didn't fix it' fixed M of S

with.label: Attempt 1 fails: same session, line-by-line walkthrough, then fix

turns.prompt: That didn't fix it. Before you change anything else, walk me through the code path this bug goes through, line by line. For each step, say what it's supposed to do and what it actually does, and stop at the first line where they differ. Then fix it.

without.label: Attempt 1 fails: same session, the plain retry line

turns.prompt: That didn't fix it. The bug is still there. Try again.
